posts.title: Pete Festersen Claims He Cut Property Taxes. Here Is the Record.
posts.excerpt: On his campaign website, Pete Festersen says 'I've cut property taxes.' Meanwhile average residential property taxes in Omaha have increased 30-40% under his leadership. He also claims North Saddle Creek as a success story.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United
posts.body:
Pete Festersen's campaign website states: 'I've cut property taxes, voted against the restaurant tax and pushed for major pension reform.'

It also says he has 'renovated the Benson, Dundee and Florence Neighborhood Business Districts and will complete North Saddle Creek this year.'

Let's look at what 'completing North Saddle Creek' has meant in practice:

- A Business Improvement District created without input from the businesses required to fund it
- Mandatory assessments collected with no transparent accounting
- A public road closed at a developer's request, now being converted to private property
- Ordinances advanced while the mayor was out of town
- A developer from Bennington — not from Saddle Creek — in control of a district that claims to represent Saddle Creek businesses

On property taxes: while Festersen claims to have cut property taxes, average residential property taxes in Omaha have increased 30 to 40 percent under his tenure. The cuts he references have disproportionately benefited corporate real estate owners. The people paying more are the residents and small business owners he claims to represent.

Now Festersen is advancing $21 million in public subsidies for a luxury apartment development at 46th and Saddle Creek that would demolish seven local businesses and replace the neighborhood's only grocery store with market-rate units starting well above what area residents can afford.

When our coalition met with Festersen and Danny Begley directly, they committed to including affordable housing, food access, and business relocation support in the development agreement. None of it appeared. What appeared instead was a new provision preventing renters from contesting property tax increases.

This is the record. Voters and neighbors should know it.

**[Visit Pete Festersen's campaign website](https://www.petefestersen.com)** and judge for yourself.

posts.title: Press Coverage: What Reporters Have Found
posts.excerpt: Local journalists have independently reported on the Saddle Creek Marketplace project. Here is what they found.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United
posts.body:
## What reporters have found

Local journalists have independently investigated the Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal. Their reporting confirms what the community has been saying.

---

### 3 News Now — Strip mall businesses face displacement from $103M development project
*December 8, 2025*

Kelly Kwon owns Lee's Beauty Supply with her husband, investing their life savings three years ago. She told 3 News Now: "We had no idea. Nobody got informed anything from our new landlord. None of us."

Mitch Hohlen of Woodsonia described both strip malls to the planning board as having "transient tenants" — businesses that have in some cases operated at these locations for over 20 years.

[Read the full story](https://www.3newsnow.com/central-omaha/central-omaha-strip-mall-businesses-face-displacement-from-103m-development-project)

---

### 3 News Now — Dundee residents weigh in on Saddle Creek Marketplace
*November 24, 2025*

Business owner Jess McCallie: "We've been seeing this all over the city, and what I'm noticing is high rent in areas with low-income earners and also little regard for community input. Feels like this is happening to us and we don't get any say."

The community organized a meeting in 48 hours after learning the TIF application had already been approved.

[Read the full story](https://www.3newsnow.com/central-omaha/dundee-residents-weigh-in-on-saddle-creek-marketplace-a-proposed-mixed-use-development)

---

### WOWT — Neighbors question $21M in public funding for luxury apartments
*January 29, 2026*

WOWT's First Alert 6 Investigations team found that Woodsonia is seeking $9 million in TIF and $12 million in EEA funding — $21 million in public subsidies — for a $110 million project with no affordable housing. The nearest grocery store to replace Family Fare would be two miles away with no direct bus service.

[Read the full story](https://www.wowt.com/2026/01/29/neighbors-question-9m-public-funding-luxury-apartments-dundee-redevelopment/)

---

### 3 News Now — City Council approves $9M financing despite pushback
*February 4, 2026*

The council voted unanimously to advance the project despite months of community opposition.

[Read the full story](https://www.3newsnow.com/central-omaha/omaha-city-council-approves-9m-financing-for-contested-dundee-development-project)

---

posts.title: WOWT: Neighbors Question $21M in Public Funding for Luxury Apartments
posts.excerpt: WOWT investigates the Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal: 223 luxury apartments, $21 million in public TIF and EEA funding, no affordable housing, and no plan to replace the grocery access being lost.
posts.author: WOWT 6 News
posts.body:
WOWT's First Alert 6 Investigations team reported on the Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal, raising questions about the use of public tax incentives for a luxury apartment development with no affordable housing.

The development would replace the Midtown Plaza shopping center at 46th and Cuming with 223 apartments and 67,000 square feet of retail space. Developer Mitch Hohlen of Woodsonia is seeking $9 million in Tax Increment Financing and $12 million in Enhanced Employment Area designation — a total of $21 million in public subsidy on a $110 million project.

Neighbor Josh Livingston told WOWT: 'At that first meeting there were conversations about whether the units were going to be affordable and their indication was that was not part of their plan.'

On the grocery gap: Family Fare's departure would leave the nearest grocery store two miles away with no direct bus service.

On the TIF: 'TIF is obviously controversial. On the one hand it's good for bringing redevelopment to the neighborhood. On the other hand you worry about who is making the most money off the TIF development.'

**[Read the full story at WOWT](https://www.wowt.com/2026/01/29/neighbors-question-9m-public-funding-luxury-apartments-dundee-redevelopment/)**

**[KETV: $103M development project near Saddle Creek Road](https://www.facebook.com/ketv7/videos/a-103-million-development-project-near-saddle-creek-road-and-northeast-of-46th-a/1565167058071517/)**

**[3 News Now: City Council approves $9M financing despite pushback](https://www.3newsnow.com/central-omaha/omaha-city-council-approves-9m-financing-for-contested-dundee-development-project)**

posts.title: 3 News Now: Strip Mall Businesses Face Displacement from $103M Development
posts.excerpt: Kelly Kwon and her husband bought Lee's Beauty Supply three years ago, investing their life savings. They had no idea their building was being demolished. 'Nobody got informed anything from our new landlord. None of us.'
posts.author: 3 News Now / KMTV
posts.body:
3 News Now reporter Jeremy Fredricks spoke directly with the business owners facing displacement. The reporting puts real names and faces to what the developer called 'transient tenants in aging buildings.'

Kelly Kwon, who owns Lee's Beauty Supply with her husband, told 3 News Now: 'We had no idea. Nobody got informed anything from our new landlord. None of us.' The couple invested their life savings buying the business three years ago, but has operated at the location for more than 20 years.

Chandra Rai, who owns Hello Nepal, has five years left on her lease and thought her business was secure. She learned about the demolition plans from news reports.

Mitch Hohlen of Woodsonia described both strip malls to the planning board as having 'transient tenants,' saying: 'We were looking at these, both of them are very tired... We saw this as an opportunity to reinvest in the area.'

Kelly Kwon's response: 'We really don't wanna get kicked out and have the rich company make the really luxury apartment to make more money so rich people get richer and the poor people get poorer. That's not really fair.'

**[Read the full story at 3 News Now](https://www.3newsnow.com/central-omaha/central-omaha-strip-mall-businesses-face-displacement-from-103m-development-project)**

posts.title: 3 News Now: Dundee Residents React to Saddle Creek Marketplace Proposal
posts.excerpt: Business owner Jess McCallie: 'We've been seeing this all over the city. High rent in areas with low-income earners and little regard for community input. Feels like this is happening to us and we don't get any say.'
posts.author: 3 News Now / KMTV
posts.body:
When Woodsonia held a community meeting about the Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal, neighbors organized in 48 hours to show up. Business owner Jess McCallie told 3 News Now:

'We've been seeing this all over the city, and what I'm noticing is high rent in areas with low-income earners and also little regard for community input. Feels like this is happening to us and we don't get any say.'

McCallie described leaving the meeting with more questions than answers: 'I feel like I have so many more questions. Partially that's a setup of the meeting structure. We only had one hour and we had a huge turnout. We organized this in only 48 hours in response to their TIF application getting approved.'

Developer Mitch Hohlen of Woodsonia described the project's goal as 'more than just housing, more than just retail, but those combined into really reinvestment in the area.' The existing grocery store building would be completely renovated, though the specific tenant to replace Family Fare remains undetermined.

**[Read the full story at 3 News Now](https://www.3newsnow.com/central-omaha/dundee-residents-weigh-in-on-saddle-creek-marketplace-a-proposed-mixed-use-development)**
